title: Hospital HMI fault acknowledgement and retry using Hospital HMI / lane UI
summary: Use the Hospital HMI / lane UI at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) to acknowledge a displayed tote workflow fault and retry the operation. In the incident case, the affected tote was confirmed as tote 28 and the site subsequently reported that all was good. Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
when_to_use: Use the Hospital HMI / lane UI at UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) when the Hospital HMI / lane UI displays a fault that blocks or interrupts a tote workflow and the affected tote can be identified with the site. This procedure is supported by the incident case for tote 28.
not_for: Do not use this as a universal resolution for every Hospital HMI / lane UI fault; the incident confirms only the documented acknowledgement and retry outcome.
Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
Do not perform undocumented HMI changes.
roles_and_responsibilities: The operator identifies the displayed fault on the Hospital HMI / lane UI, confirms the affected tote with the site, acknowledges the fault, retries the operation, and verifies the resulting tote workflow state.
Escalate when the fault remains after acknowledgement and retry or when the affected tote cannot be confirmed.
safety_notes: Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
Stop rather than perform undocumented changes if the fault cannot be cleared.
access_or_tools_needed: Site confirmation of the affected tote ID

access_required: Operator access to the Hospital HMI / lane UI
system_preconditions: A fault is displayed on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
The site can confirm the affected tote ID before retry.

visual_references.description: Embedded Hospital HMI / lane UI screenshot from case 218550 page 12. The image shows a small HMI-like tote screen with a red header and green list fields; most text is unreadable. Use it to orient to the displayed fault and tote workflow area.

steps.title: Locate the displayed fault on the Hospital HMI / lane UI
steps.purpose: Identify the active Hospital HMI / lane UI fault and the associated tote workflow before taking recovery action.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, locate the displayed fault and the affected tote workflow area.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI / lane UI shows the fault condition and an associated tote workflow that can be identified for confirmation.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI displays the relevant tote workflow without an unrelated or unidentified fault being selected.
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI fault or affected tote workflow cannot be located or identified.

actions.label: Inspect fault screen
actions.exact_action: Locate the displayed fault associated with the affected tote on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the displayed fault or affected tote workflow cannot be identified.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The HMI at the hospital is showing a fault.

steps.title: Confirm the affected tote ID
steps.purpose: Ensure the acknowledgement and retry are applied to the tote involved in the displayed Hospital HMI / lane UI fault.
steps.instruction: Before retrying on the Hospital HMI / lane UI, ask the site to confirm the affected tote ID. For this incident case, confirm that it is tote 28.
steps.expected_result: The site confirms that the affected tote at the Hospital HMI / lane UI is tote 28.
steps.healthy_condition: The tote ID shown or identified in the Hospital HMI / lane UI matches the site confirmation of tote 28.
steps.failure_condition: The site cannot confirm the tote ID, or the identified tote does not match tote 28.

actions.label: Confirm tote identity
actions.exact_action: Confirm with the site that the affected tote is ID 28 before retrying the Hospital HMI / lane UI operation.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the affected tote cannot be confirmed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Yes the tote at hospital is 28.

steps.title: Acknowledge the fault and retry the tote operation
steps.purpose: Clear the displayed Hospital HMI / lane UI fault through the documented acknowledgement and retry action.
steps.instruction: On the Hospital HMI / lane UI, select the displayed acknowledge control and try the tote operation again. Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
steps.expected_result: The Hospital HMI / lane UI accepts the acknowledgement and the tote operation enters a retry attempt rather than remaining blocked by the same acknowledged fault.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI responds to the acknowledge control and the affected tote workflow proceeds into the retry.
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI does not accept the acknowledgement, the retry cannot be started, or the same fault continues to block the tote workflow.

actions.label: Acknowledge and retry
actions.exact_action: Hit acknowledge and try again on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
Stop if the fault remains after acknowledge and retry.
Stop if the tote cannot proceed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Small HMI-like tote screen associated with the reported HMI fault.

steps.title: Verify the Hospital HMI / lane UI workflow is no longer blocked
steps.purpose: Confirm that the acknowledgement and retry restored the affected tote workflow on the Hospital HMI / lane UI.
steps.instruction: Review the affected tote workflow on the Hospital HMI / lane UI after the retry and ask the site to confirm the resulting condition.
steps.expected_result: The affected tote workflow is no longer blocked by the displayed fault, and the site reports that the condition is all good.
steps.healthy_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI shows the affected tote workflow in a progressing or otherwise non-blocked state, with no continuing fault preventing the workflow.
steps.failure_condition: The Hospital HMI / lane UI still blocks the tote workflow, shows the fault again, or the site cannot confirm a good condition.

actions.label: Verify workflow recovery
actions.exact_action: Verify that the fault no longer blocks the tote workflow on the Hospital HMI / lane UI and confirm that the site reports the condition as all good.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the fault cannot be cleared or the affected tote cannot proceed.
Stop if the site cannot confirm the resulting condition.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Yes the tote at hospital is 28. Yes Sir all good.

success_criteria: The site confirms that the affected tote on the Hospital HMI / lane UI is tote 28.
The Hospital HMI / lane UI acknowledge control accepts the fault acknowledgement.
The retry proceeds without the fault continuing to block the tote workflow.
The site confirms that the condition is all good.
healthy_conditions: The Hospital HMI / lane UI displays the affected tote workflow without a continuing blocking fault.
The affected tote workflow proceeds after acknowledgement and retry.
The site confirms a good operating condition.
failure_conditions: The fault remains after acknowledgement and retry.
The affected tote cannot be confirmed as tote 28.
The affected tote workflow cannot proceed.
The site cannot confirm that the condition is all good.
escalation_guidance: Escalate for further support if the Hospital HMI / lane UI fault cannot be cleared after acknowledgement and retry.
Escalate if the affected tote cannot be confirmed or cannot proceed.
Do not unplug the Hospital HMI / lane UI or perform undocumented changes.
